# --since lists the targets whose inputs changed since a commit, staged,
# unstaged or untracked, and those depending on their content.
exec git init -q
exec git add .
exec git -c user.email=test@example.com -c user.name=Test commit -qm base

cp a.txt.changed a.txt
exec git add a.txt
cp e.txt.changed e.txt
cp d.txt.new d.txt

! bit --list --since HEAD
stderr '--since requires -ll'

bit -ll --since HEAD
! stdout '\A\s'
stdout 'a \('
stdout 'c \('
stdout 'd \('
stdout 'e \('
! stdout 'b \('
cp stdout since-head.txt

# Without a commit, --since compares with the remote's default branch.
exec git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/master HEAD
exec git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD refs/remotes/origin/master
bit -ll --since
cmp stdout since-head.txt

bit -ll --since c
stdout 'c \('
! stdout 'e \('

-- BUILD.bit --
a = exec {
  command = "true"
  inputs = ["a.txt"]
}

b = exec {
  command = "true"
  inputs = ["b.txt"]
}

c = exec {
  command = "true"
  inputs = ["c.txt"]
  depends_on = [a]
}

d = exec {
  command = "true"
  inputs = ["d.txt"]
}

e = exec {
  command = "true"
  inputs = ["e.txt"]
}
-- a.txt --
a
-- b.txt --
b
-- c.txt --
c
-- e.txt --
e
-- a.txt.changed --
changed
-- e.txt.changed --
changed
-- d.txt.new --
untracked
